original_test_intent: Validate that DCGM level-4 diagnostics can access required GPU devices and services under the approved OS permissions and security policy, without unapproved privilege or policy bypass.
original_method: Record OS/kernel, execution identity, groups, ACL/capabilities, device-node ownership, container boundaries and SELinux/AppArmor state; preserve logs; validate least-required privileges; establish supported service/persistence state; run the full level-4 suite; attribute permission/OS-block results; confirm policy is unchanged and restore runtime state.
manual_activity: OS security and GPU owners approve the execution identity, minimal device/service privileges and expected blocked-versus-allowed matrix; operator controls the isolated maintenance run.
required_inputs: Container and SELinux/AppArmor scope where applicable
Isolation, OOB, stop limits and recovery
safety_requirements: Do not weaken security policy merely to obtain PASS
Never embed credentials or disable host verification
Preserve complete audit and diagnostic evidence
Bound privileged commands to approved identity and devices
Restore runtime state; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Inventory effective identity and GPU access
Run one complete level-4 diagnostic in approved context
Map permission denials, skips and subtests
Confirm policy unchanged and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve privilege/access matrix and expected denials
Resolve service/diagnostic level and stop policy

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It invokes DCGM but defeats the security focus through credential exposure and host-key bypass, omits effective permission checks and truncates evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use authenticated least-privilege access, record effective IDs/device ACLs/security enforcement, then execute the approved full level-4 test after service initialization.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Persistence enablement, source level 4, 120-minute allowance and all-tests-PASS criterion remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Evaluate required operations against a predeclared least-privilege matrix and distinguish expected policy denials from diagnostic defects using full audit and DCGM evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity, device-node, LSM/container and audit evidence plus an unchanged-policy postcheck.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Running as unrestricted root can hide permission defects and cannot validate OS Blocks behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Changing ACLs, capabilities or security enforcement can create a wider security regression than the diagnostic itself.

project_override_considerations: Security engineering must decide whether the case is expected to succeed under a service account, root, or containerized context and enumerate any intentionally blocked actions.
expected_evidence: GPU device-node ACL and SELinux/AppArmor/container context
Full level-4 permission-related subtests, denials, skips and exit
Unchanged final security policy/runtime state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Procedure places service start after diagnostic execution, DeepSeek substitutes level-1 evidence for level 4, and the source gives no permission/OS-block acceptance matrix despite the title.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; execution blocks only if approved security context, required access matrix, supported level/order, isolation or recovery is unavailable.

review_improvement: Makes the permission test falsifiable without weakening the controls it is intended to validate.
independent_technical_reasoning: A root-run diagnostic may pass precisely because it bypasses the permission boundary under test. The correct oracle compares each required DCGM operation with an approved access matrix, records expected and unexpected denials, and verifies that no ACL, capability or security policy was broadened for convenience.
